newsitem.title: USA: General Cigar sizzles at Wall Street debut.
newsitem.headline: General Cigar sizzles at Wall Street debut.

text.p: General Cigar Holdings Inc., the nation's largest manufacturer of brand name premium cigars, made a fiery debut on Friday, with its stock surging about 31 percent in heavy trading.
The stock, which was priced at the top of its estimated range of $16 to $18, rose $5 to close at $23 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the sixth most active issue.

Demand was so strong that the price of General Cigar's six million Class A shares was raised from an initial estimate of $14 to $16 per share earlier in the week, according to underwriter Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities.

"This (cigar smoking) is not a passing fad," said David Menlow, president of Springfield, N.J.-based IPO Financial Network Corp. "I see it lasting till there is some increased effort on the part of the FDA to deter people from cigar smoking."
Moreover, he said, "there's a lot of ego involved in this (cigar) business," and something that allows people to pamper their egos won't disappear all that quickly.
Steven Tuen, an analyst at IPO Value Monitor, is more sceptical about the industry's long-term prospects. "We think that this is a fad," which could burn out over five years, he said.
However, based on the heavy backlog for premium cigars -- the segment in which General Cigar has the most exposure -- the company should do "pretty well over the next year or two," Tuen said.
Founded in 1906, General Cigar makes top selling cigar brands such as Macanudo and Partagas, and operates the New York City cigar bar "Club Macanudo."
The New York-based company had net sales of $196.7 million and operating profit of $32.3 million in fiscal 1996, after acquisition-related expenses.
General Cigar's parent company, Culbro Corp., holds all of the shares of its Class B common stock. Each Class B share represents 10 votes, whereas each Class A share represents one vote.

According to the company's filing, Culbro will be merged into General Cigar after the closing of the offering, and about 20 million of the company's Class B shares will be issued to Culbro shareholders.

Additionally, Culbro's non-tobacco business is to be transferred to a new company, so that General Cigar will hold all of the cigar and tobacco assets, and another company which will hold all of the non-tobacco assets.
According to a company spokesman, the non-tobacco company, to be spun-off to shareholders of Culbro, will be known as "Griffen Land and Nursery Corp".
Vistana Inc. and First Aviation Services Inc. also made their debuts on Wall Street Friday, with Vistana garnering a premium and First Aviation falling below its initial public offering price.

Vistana, a developer and operator of timeshare resorts in the United States, offered 5.5 million shares in a deal led by Montgomery Securities. The shares priced at $12, at the lower end of a $12 to $14 range, and moved up $2.625 to $14.625 on Nasdaq.

First Aviation's shares priced at $10, also at the bottom of their estimated range, and closed 25 cents lower at $9.75 on Nasdaq. The company, which provides services to operators of military, commercial and general aviation aircraft engines, offered 3.9 million shares. Smith Barney was lead underwriter on the deal.
